profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility, internally identified in public records as Austin 3, is located at 1801 East 6th Street, Austin, TX 78702, in Travis County, a separate building from the Smith School Road Lumen Austin 1 facility also tracked in this registry; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Texas's data center sales tax exemption cost the state roughly $5-30 million a year from 2014 through 2022, jumped to more than $150 million in 2023, and is now projected at $1.3 billion for the current fiscal year, $3.2 billion over 2026-2028, and nearly $1.8 billion annually by fiscal 2030, according to the Texas Tribune. Separately, ERCOT's interconnection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts of pending requests, more than five times the grid's record peak demand, with Governor Abbott stating about 90% of new power requests are data centers; Abbott ordered an audit of queued data centers in August 2026, and ERCOT sought a delay of its transmission planning study from the Public Utility Commission the same month.

reading.body:
Lumen Austin 3 is a carrier-neutral colocation facility in downtown Austin that Lumen operates as part of a network-edge product rather than a hyperscale campus. Lumen does not publish power capacity, square footage, or rack count for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites, including this one, so its absolute size cannot be determined from operator disclosures. The facility offers cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range, which serves traditional enterprise and carrier tenants rather than the 30 to 80 kilowatt per-rack densities typical of AI training clusters.

Austin 3 sits in a state where 18 facilities have published power specs totaling 468 MW, making Texas rank second nationally in disclosed hyperscale capacity. This facility is not among those 18 and contributes no disclosed capacity to that total. Texas now holds 133 mapped data centers, yet the gap between mapped count and published specs reflects that most facilities, including this Lumen property, operate under opacity that prevents comparison to wholesale campuses where AI compute concentrates.

Texas faces a grid constraint that will sharply limit further AI scaling regardless of colocation availability. ERCOT's interconnection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts of pending requests, more than five times the grid's record peak demand, with Governor Abbott stating about 90 percent of new power requests are data centers. Lumen's edge colocation model, designed for distributed enterprise workloads rather than consolidated AI training, does not position this facility as material to the compute scaling problem The World of AI tracks.
